target_audience_note: The document names no audience category. It defines the insured persons under Division A as “The persons designated under the special conditions who are involved in the design and construction of the insured structure, as well as the seller of the buildings”.
summary: Insurance product information document (IPID) for APROBAT decennial civil liability, published under the header “LALUX Assurances - Product : APROBAT decennial CL”. Division A insures the decennial civil liability owed by the persons involved in the design and construction of the insured structure to the owner or purchaser under articles 1792 and 2270 of the Civil Code; Division B insures their liability to the owner, purchaser or third parties under articles 1382, 1383, 1384 and 1386 of the Luxembourg Civil Code for bodily injury, material and immaterial damage that results from an accident covered by Division A. Damage to major structures is covered for 10 years and minor structures (radiators, doors, windows, etc.) for 2 years. The cover is conditional on the works being overseen by an approved inspection body.

coverages.name: Division A - Decennial civil liability insurance for the owner or purchaser
coverages.description: The policy guarantees the insured persons the financial compensation to which they may be liable to the owner or purchaser of the structure pursuant to articles 1792 and 2270 of the Civil Code. Article 1792 : If the building becomes damaged in whole or in part by the defect of the construction, the architects, contractors and other persons bound to the owner by a service contract shall be liable for it for 10 years. Damage to major structures is covered for 10 years, while minor structures (radiators, doors, windows, etc.) are covered for 2 years. The insurance covers damage such as moisture on basement walls or plaster cracks.

gaps: UNFINISHED EDITORIAL PLACEHOLDER, PRINTED ON THE PAGE. The section “How do I cancel the contract ?” (page 2) contains no cancellation terms. It prints two lines of instructions to whoever was drafting the document: “- Decide what to write, as the cancellation terms are different (single premium, etc.).” and “- E.g. Cancellation is possible within 30 days of receipt of the contract documents”. This was verified against a 2.4x render of page 2: both lines are genuinely printed inside the grey box under the section heading, in the same body font as the rest of the document, and are not a text-layer artefact. The “30 days” figure is introduced by “E.g.” and must NOT be read as this product’s cancellation period. duration_and_cancellation.notice_period and methods are therefore left null.

NO LEGAL ENTITY NAMED: the document identifies the insurer only as the brand “LALUX Assurances” in the header band (“LALUX Assurances - Product : APROBAT decennial CL”) and as “the Insurer” in the body. No company name, no legal form, no RCS number and no address appear anywhere on either page. insurer_name carries the task metadata value “lalux” and is not a reading of the document.
NO EDITION DATE: neither page prints an edition date, a version number, an internal reference or a dated footer; a 2.4x render of both full pages confirms it. edition_date and reference remain null.

TITLE vs CONTENT: the printed title is “APROBAT - Decennial civil liability” and the product line reads “APROBAT decennial CL” - the biennial limb does not appear in the title. The body nevertheless states “Damage to major structures is covered for 10 years, while minor structures (radiators, doors, windows, etc.) are covered for 2 years” and cites “articles 1792 and 2270 of the Civil Code”. Article 1792 is quoted in full; article 2270, which carries the two-year limb, is cited but its text is NOT reproduced.

“WHAT IS INSURED ?” OPENS ON A SERVICE, NOT A GUARANTEE: the first paragraph of that box describes the APROBAT inspection service (“APROBAT checks whether the construction complies with the rules of good workmanship... For constructions with a value of less than EUR 1.5 million, APROBAT carries out all the mandatory site inspections.”). It has been recorded as a coverage entry because that is where the document prints it, but it describes an inspection service and the document does not say it is an insured guarantee.

ONLY ONE MONETARY FIGURE: “EUR 1.5 million” (page 1), and it is a threshold for the scope of the APROBAT site inspections, not a sum insured or a limit of indemnity. No sum insured, no limit of indemnity, no deductible and no premium amount is printed; deductibles remains null. The only other quantified values are percentages and periods: 25 %, 10 years, 2 years, 15-day period, two months, 30 days (in the placeholder line only).

SUMS INSURED AND RISK LOCATION LEFT TO THE SPECIAL CONDITIONS: “Where am I covered ?” answers only “Specified risk situation(s) in the Special Conditions.”, and the insured persons, the sums insured and the deductibles are all referred to the special conditions, which do not accompany this document.

GENERAL CONDITIONS REFERENCED BUT NOT IDENTIFIED: the document refers three times to the “General Conditions” (the “Technical inspection” section and paragraph, and the disclaimer) without giving a reference, an edition date or a location. No English-language general conditions accompany this IPID.

THE “ARE THERE ANY RESTRICTIONS ON COVER ?” BOX holds four items that are not exclusions: a waiting period, an optional extension, a sub-limit and a reduction of the sum insured. They have been placed in waiting_periods, coverages (is_optional true), sub_limits and limits respectively, and the box is also preserved verbatim in special_conditions so that the document’s own structure survives. They were deliberately NOT added to exclusions.
